title: Article prompt screen: baseline versus revised instructions

design.effort: Preserve captured client defaults: Luna medium, 6.1 Sol low; identical within each model across prompts and repeats. Graders 6.1 Sol Ultra.
design.grader: Fresh GPT-6.1 Sol Ultra agent per case; identities and prompt variants withheld.

candidateBar.predeclared: Exploratory screen only. A Luna production candidate needs zero fatal source errors in revised drafts and mean content score within 3 points of revised Sol, with no material citation regression. Raw usability and repair costs remain separate; no default adoption from this screen.

deliveryExclusions.reason: Delivery-only exclusion: did not read input-10.txt, omitting the final four frozen transcript segments. No quality-based exclusion; all original evidence and usage retained.

accounting.excludes: Parent/orchestration, prompt-author helper and independent verification helper; includes delivery retry attempt costs. No Codex bill or production cost claim.

independentAccountingAudit.pricingMethod: Independent Decimal calculation from pricing-snapshot.json; ordinary input excludes cache reads and writes, reasoning is already included in output, and the >272000 multiplier is applied per response.

pricing.longContextRule: For each request above 272000 input tokens, double input/cache rates and multiply output rates by 1.5. Do not apply this threshold to cumulative agent usage.
pricing.accounting: Sum individually priced response token_usage_record.usage records. Ordinary input excludes cache reads/writes. Reasoning output is already included in output_tokens. Cache writes are reported separately.
pricing.limitations: These are API-equivalent costs for Codex activity, not an API bill, a Codex allowance valuation, or a production forecast.

sources.title: 90 minutes of unfiltered product advice from Snap and Discord’s product chief | Peter Sellis
OpenAI Dev Day 2026: The releases that actually matter

limits: Two samples per cell and five selected difficult public recordings do not estimate general production failure rates.
Prompt was developed from earlier failures; held-outs were unseen by its author.
Codex system/tools/cache differ from production; no server-enforced structured decoding or automatic quote repair.
No measured production cost per accepted article.
One grader model; no human adjudication.
Held-out Rotterdam transcript has substantial mixed-language artifacts; dominant-language assessment is less certain.
Uncached final-response sensitivity removes recorded cache discounts but retains the Codex system/tool context; it is still not a production forecast.
privacy: Aggregate and numeric evidence only; no accounts, job/session/response identifiers, machine paths, transcripts or raw drafts.
